title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops & Top Support Issues
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary

This page is the canonical Developer Experience (DevEx) playbook for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. It provides standards, recommended structure, maintenance checklists, and a curated list of common user problems and their fixes so engineers and technical writers can ship consistent, high-quality developer docs and ship-first-time success.

Audience

- Technical Writers (Docs)
- Developer Experience Engineers
- SDK Owners
- Support and Solutions Engineering

Scope

Covers the public-facing SDK guides, quickstarts and templates included in the Docs site, standard API examples (JS/Python/CLI), the docs-site operating procedures for publishing and releases, and the canonical support issue list for the top recurring integration problems. Does NOT cover internal runbooks or infra-level SRE playbooks (see eng-platform/ and eng-sre/ for those).

1) Principles and Standards

- Be concise and example-first: each guide should have a one-paragraph explanation and a minimal copy-paste example that returns results in < 60s for a new user.
- Provide a graduated path: Quickstart -> Integration Example -> Production Hardening.
- Include explicit troubleshooting steps and link to the canonical support issues below.
- Keep API examples synchronized with the SDK changelog (see release checklist).

2) Docs structure and required sections for every SDK guide

Each SDK guide (JS, Python, Go, Java, and HTTP/CLI) must include the following sections in this order:

- Title (short, action-oriented)
- One-line summary
- Why/When to use this SDK
- Quickstart (copy/paste runnable example)
- Installation and version pinning
- Auth and configuration (environment variables, KMS hints for private deployments)
- Key concepts and short glossary (e.g., request vs streaming response, token counting)
- Full API reference links (auto-generated)
- Example patterns (prompts, retries, streaming consumption, tool-calling)
- Troubleshooting (link to the canonical issues table below)
- Migration notes for breaking changes
- Contributing guide for SDK owners

3) Quickstarts & Templates (recommended templates)

Create language-specific quickstarts with the following recommended templates:

- quickstart-minimal: single-file example that does text generation using a Redwood-hosted model (<= 20 lines).
- quickstart-chat-flow: chat client demonstrating streaming + function/tool calling.
- quickstart-embeddings: embedding generation, local similarity search example (FAISS snippet).
- quickstart-batch: shows batching and retry patterns for Dedicated customers.
- template-service: a minimal microservice template (Dockerfile, k8s manifest fragment) that uses the SDK and best-practice timeouts and retry backoffs.

Each template must include:
- README with expected outputs
- Dockerfile and manifest examples (where applicable)
- CI snippet for running quickstart smoke tests

4) API Examples (canonical snippets to include in docs)

Provide short, copy-paste examples for the following scenarios in each supported language:

- Basic text generation (non-streaming)
- Streaming generation (consume token stream and render progressively)
- Function / tool-calling example (JSON schema + function handler)
- Embeddings + similarity search (with small local index example)
- Error handling and retry pattern with exponential backoff
- Authorization using API Key and example for using KMS-wrapped keys in Private deployments

Canonical JavaScript example (minimal):

```javascript
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/gpt-3o', prompt: 'Translate to French: Hello, world' });
console.log(res.text);
```

Canonical Python example (minimal):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(model='redwood/gpt-3o', prompt='Summarize: Quarterly financials')
print(resp.text)
```

CLI example (curl):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-3o","prompt":"List 3 KPIs for support"}'
```

5) Docs-site Operating Procedures (publishing & release workflow)

This section defines the minimal checklist for releasing SDK docs and quickstarts. The Docs site is the single source-of-truth; follow this workflow:

Steps to publish (numbered):
1. Author creates PR in docs repo (docs/contents/<language>/<topic>). Include smoke test script that runs the quickstart.
2. Assign reviewer from the SDK owner team and one Docs reviewer. Add label: docs-ready.
3. CI runs: build, linter, quickstart smoke tests (containerized).
4. When CI passes, author merges and triggers automated extraction to the site (Netlify/Next).
5. Post-merge: SDK owner posts a change summary in #devex-docs with links to the PR and smoke test results.
6. If the change touches API examples, update the API examples checksum in the SDK changelog file (docs/scripts/update_examples_checksum.sh).
7. For breaking changes: schedule a migration notice and coordinate with support and marketing (at least 7 days prior).

Ownership and SLAs:
- Docs changes must be reviewed within 48 business hours.
- Smoke tests must complete within 15 minutes in CI.

6) Maintenance checklist (monthly)

- Run the examples smoke test job for all quickstarts (automated) and resolve any failures within 7 days.
- Validate SDK version compatibility matrix (update table below).
- Re-run the API examples checksum job and reconcile diffs.
- Archive quickstarts that have < 5 uses in telemetry for 6+ months and notify SDK owners.

7) Top support issues and canonical fixes

Below are the top recurring issues reported to Support & Solutions Engineering for SDKs and Docs. Each entry lists symptoms, root cause (typical), and the canonical fix or mitigation that should be added to the troubleshooting section of the relevant docs.

Issue 1: Authentication failures (401 / invalid_api_key)
- Symptom: Clients receive 401 on first request after SDK install or after rotating keys.
- Typical root cause: Missing or malformed REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, or using an expired/rotated key. In Private deployments: misconfigured KMS wrapper.
- Canonical fix: 1) Verify environment variable is set: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY`. 2) Try an explicit header with curl to rule out SDK env parsing. 3) For rotated keys, ensure deployed services have updated secrets (k8s secret rollout). 4) For KMS-wrapped keys, confirm KMS IAM bindings and that the client SDK can unwrap tokens. Add snippet showing explicit header usage.

Issue 2: Streaming output stalls / incomplete streams
- Symptom: Client receives initial tokens then no further messages; connection remains open.
- Typical root cause: Improper streaming consumption (not draining the async iterator), intermediary proxies (nginx/ALB) cutting idle connections, or missing chunked transfer encoding headers.
- Canonical fix: 1) Show minimal streaming consumer pattern (JS/Python) that fully drains the stream. 2) Recommend keepalive and proxy config: `proxy_read_timeout 120s; proxy_send_timeout 120s; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`. 3) For serverless front-ends, recommend using WebSockets or a streaming-capable gateway.

Issue 3: High token usage / unexpectedly large bills
- Symptom: Customers report skyrocketing token usage compared to expectations.
- Typical root cause: Default prompt templates include developer debug content, missing stop sequences, or accidental echoing loops in prompt engineering. Also common: clients using long context windows without chunking.
- Canonical fix: 1) Add token-counting examples with conservative token budgets. 2) Document `max_tokens` defaults per SDK and show how to enforce stop sequences. 3) Recommend using embeddings + similarity search for retrieval use-cases instead of repeatedly sending long documents.

Issue 4: Slow cold-start latency for Dedicated pools
- Symptom: First request after inactivity has 3–10x higher latency.
- Typical root cause: Warm pool scaling or container start-up (model loading), cache misses on KV cache.
- Canonical fix: 1) Explain expected cold-start profile and offer configuration knobs: `min_replicas`, `warmup_policy: preheat`. 2) For Dedicated customers, provide a small snippet showing a synthetic warmup job. 3) For Hosted customers, recommend prewarming via a keepalive ping job.

Issue 5: Inconsistent outputs across SDK versions
- Symptom: Same prompt returns different outputs after SDK upgrade.
- Typical root cause: SDK wrapper changed default tokenization or post-processing (e.g., trimming, whitespace normalization), or implicit model version change in the model alias.
- Canonical fix: 1) Always pin model and SDK versions in examples. 2) Provide a migration guide listing behavioral changes for each SDK release.

Troubleshooting quick-reference table (text table)

| Symptom | Likely cause | First action | Link to doc |
|---|---|---|---|
| 401 auth error | Missing/rotated key | Verify env var; curl test | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/auth-troubleshooting |
| Streaming stalls | Proxy idle timeout | Test direct to API; adjust proxy timeouts | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/streaming-best-practices |
| High token usage | Missing stop sequences | Add `max_tokens`; add token-counting example | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/token-budgeting |
| Cold start latency | Pool scaling/model load | Increase min_replicas; warmup job | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/warmup-patterns |

8) Release checklist for SDK docs and examples

- Update SDK changelog with example checksum and versions.
- Update quickstart smoke test and verify it passes in CI for target language.
- Run the examples linter (checks for secrets, PII, and unstable timestamps).
- Add or update migration note if there are breaking changes.
- Notify #devex-docs and #support 48 hours before major changes.

9) Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: DevEx team (eng-developer-experience). Secondary owners: SDK owners for each language.
- For recurring support issues that require infra changes, escalate to eng-platform with a P1 analysis ticket.

Appendix: Example config tables and version matrix

SDK compatibility matrix (example):

| SDK | Supported site version | Minimum SDK version | Recommended pin |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| JavaScript | docs-site v2.3 | >= 1.4.0 | 1.6.2 |
| Python | docs-site v2.3 | >= 2.0.0 | 2.1.0 |
| Go | docs-site v2.3 | >= 0.9.0 | 1.0.1 |

Environment variables and example values:

- REDWOOD_API_KEY: example-key-xxxxxxxx
- REDWOOD_ENV: production | staging
- REDWOOD_REGION: us-west-2

Common CI snippet (bash) for quickstart smoke test:

```bash
set -e
cd quickstart-minimal
# install and run the quickstart inside a virtual env / container
./ci/run_smoke_test.sh
```
